root_cause.text: The `v9fs_apply_options` function uses bitwise OR to apply mount flags from parsed options without first clearing the existing access mode bits, causing incompatible flags to accumulate and match no valid access mode.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (ctx->session_opts.flags & V9FS_ACCESS_MASK) v9ses->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;` before the OR assignment, explicitly clearing the access mask to prevent bit accumulation. The commit message explains that `v9fs_session_init` sets `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT` as default, and user-provided `access=user` adds `V9FS_ACCESS_USER` via OR, resulting in both bits set, which falls through to default `INVALID_UID` in `v9fs_fid_lookup`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear existing access mask flags before OR-ing new session option flags to prevent default flags from persisting incorrectly.
intent_record.what: Added an if-statement that clears the V9FS_ACCESS_MASK bits from v9ses->flags when ctx->session_opts.flags has any of those bits set, before OR-ing the new flags.
intent_record.how: This prevents the old default access flags from persisting alongside newly specified access flags, ensuring that only the intended access mode is active.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `v9fs_apply_options`, the line `v9ses->flags |= ctx->session_opts.flags;` (line ~220) ORs the parsed flags onto the existing flags without first clearing the access mode bits. The initial flags set in `v9fs_session_init` include `V9FS_ACCESS_USER`, and the parsed flags have exactly one access mode (e.g., `V9FS_ACCESS_ANY`). The OR operation leaves both bits set, creating an invalid combination that matches no valid access mode. This matches the root cause: 'bitwise OR to apply mount flags from parsed options without first clearing the existing access mode bits'.
